report.scope: Unit-dose pods for ordinary US washers. Liquid, powder and sheets appear only as price benchmarks. Prices are Walmart search-page prices unless noted; Kirkland comes from a third-party tracker.

primer.what_it_is: A pod is PVA (water-soluble polymer) film holding a surfactant/enzyme concentrate. Multi-chamber designs separate oxidizers and enzymes from the liquid. Fill weight varies roughly 2x between brands.

must_haves.why: Net-weight line ÷ count is verifiable on the label and is the real denominator.
On the back panel; shows whether 1 pod is enough for your loads.

verdict.headline: Buy selectively: Kirkland or Tide at the 22–27¢ knee; pay 44¢ only if you'd use 2 pods.
verdict.confidence: Low-moderate: only about 8 products priced, one retailer, no CR pod table, no price history.
verdict.reasoning: Kirkland (~13¢/pod) is the value floor, but its pod stain scores are unverified. Tide at 22–27¢ has the strongest lab results. Above ~27¢ you pay for scent, marketing or heavier fill.
verdict.price_watch_summary: No sale or historical prices were seen; thresholds are judgment calls. Kirkland ≤~$19; Tide Free & Gentle 102 ct <~$22; Tide PODS 76 ct at $19.94 or ~$17 on sale; Gain Flings <~$12 or skip; Tide Power PODS 45 ct wait for ~$16; A&H $9.12 buy-whenever.

normalization.unit: Cost per effective wash (pods needed × price per pod), cross-checked with dollars per ounce of fill
normalization.unit_rationale: Count is set by the manufacturer and fill varies ~2x: Tide Power PODS ~1.47 oz per pod, Gain Flings ~0.67 oz, A&H Paks ~0.70 oz, Kirkland ~0.84 oz. Ounce figures are derived from Walmart per-lb prices, not label numbers. Per-ounce alone also misleads because dose rules differ.
normalization.quality_adjustment: Value = stain-removal score ÷ cost per effective wash, with a hard-water penalty (CR: hard water degrades performance) and a dissolution/residue penalty (film left in cold or short cycles forces a rewash, weighed most). No full numeric score: CR's pod table was not retrieved.
normalization.formula: Cost per effective wash = pods per load × price per pod. Assume 1 pod for a normal load, 2 for heavy or large loads with thinner-fill products. Value = stain-removal score ÷ cost per wash, minus hard-water and residue penalties.

normalization.size_economics: Larger packs cost less per pod: Kirkland 152 ct ~12.5–13¢ vs Tide Free & Gentle 102 ct 24.5¢ vs Tide PODS 76 ct 26.2¢. Subscribe and multi-pack deals were not verified. Check Tide PODS 76 ct fill before buying (35¢/oz implies ~0.75 oz per pod).

diminishing_returns.knee_example: Tide Free & Gentle 102 ct at $24.94 (24.5¢ per pod) or Tide PODS Original 76 ct at $19.94 (26.2¢). Knee range is about 22–27¢ per pod.
diminishing_returns.below_knee: Below ~13¢ you leave warehouse-club pricing for the store-brand tier. Kirkland pod stain scores unconfirmed; one Reddit thread title reports a formula change and visibly smaller pods (thread unread).
diminishing_returns.above_knee: Above ~27¢ you pay for scent-boost and marketing (Gain Flings) or larger fill (Power PODS 44.3¢). Best tested performance costs about 3x Kirkland; the buyer decides if it is worth it.

consensus.expert_view: CR names Tide Hygienic Clean Heavy Duty 10X and Tide Ultra Oxi Power Pods best pods; GH picks Tide Hygienic Clean. Jeeves NY scored Tide Hygienic Clean pods 100, Tide Original liquid 92.7, Persil 62.6. CR says sheets are too weak to recommend.
consensus.community_view: Only Reddit thread title found (unreadable): people noticed a Kirkland formula change and visibly smaller pods. Launderwise, a compiler not a lab, says Tide evo tiles are the sheet exception.
consensus.where_they_disagree: Tide vs Persil: Reviewed prefers Persil; Wirecutter has Persil as runner-up to Tide among liquids. CR's Kirkland best-value verdict is confirmed for the liquid only, not pods. CR's pod table was not retrieved.
